def: having no chance of success; producing no useful result no matter how much effort is made

def: present everywhere and spreading through every part of a place, group, or system

note: Often describes something unwelcome, such as a smell, a problem, or an attitude.

def: so small or unimportant that it is not worth considering
ex: The price difference between the two brands was negligible, so Priya bought the one she liked.

def: treating all sides equally and fairly, without favoring one person or group

cloze.s: Because the referee's brother played for one of the teams, fans doubted he could be ___.

def: excellent enough to serve as a model that others should copy

cloze.s: Her ___ attendance, without a single absence in four years, earned a special mention at graduation.

def: having plenty of money and a comfortable standard of living; wealthy

def: drawn from many different styles, sources, or types rather than following just one
ex: Wei has eclectic taste in music, from opera to hip-hop to Brazilian samba.

cloze.s: The festival's ___ lineup mixed jazz, country, punk, and classical acts.

def: perfectly clean, neat, or tidy, with no marks, dirt, or mistakes
ex: Olga keeps her kitchen immaculate, wiping every counter after each meal.

cloze.s: After the cleaning crew left, the hotel room was ___, without a speck of dust anywhere.

def: lasting or staying only a short time; not permanent

def: directly related to the matter being discussed or considered; relevant

def: standing out so clearly that it is easily seen or noticed
ex: Liam's bright orange jacket made him conspicuous in the crowd of dark suits.

cloze.s: The new glass tower is so ___ that you can spot it from almost anywhere in the city.

def: clever, original, and inventive, especially in solving a problem
ex: Yuki came up with an ingenious way to store bikes on the ceiling of her tiny apartment.

cloze.s: Her ___ trick of turning an old shoe box into a phone stand impressed everyone at the office.

note: Not the same as *ingenuous*, which means innocent and trusting.

def: stating opinions openly and boldly, even when they may upset or offend others
ex: Malik is an outspoken critic of the city's plan to close the library.

cloze.s: Sofia was the most ___ person at the meeting, openly challenging the manager's proposal in front of everyone.

def: kind, generous, and wanting to help or do good for others
ex: A benevolent neighbor paid for the family's groceries after the fire.

cloze.s: The ___ donor anonymously paid off the school lunch debts of every student in the district.

def: causing strong disagreement that splits people into opposing sides
ex: The proposal to close the park became a divisive issue in the neighborhood.

cloze.s: The talk-show host is a ___ figure, adored by half his audience and despised by the other half.

def: irregular and unpredictable, changing often with no clear pattern
ex: The car's erratic movements made other drivers suspect the driver was falling asleep.
Fatima's erratic work schedule makes it hard to plan weekends with friends.

cloze.s: The old printer's behavior is ___: it works perfectly one day and jams constantly the next.

def: absolutely necessary; too important to do without
ex: A good map app is indispensable when traveling in an unfamiliar city.
Tomas became indispensable to the team because he understood every system.

cloze.s: For long-distance hikers, a reliable water filter is ___; nobody sets out without one.

def: so foolish or unreasonable that it is laughable
ex: Charging fifty dollars for parking at a high school game is ludicrous.

cloze.s: The idea that a cat could open the safe by itself was so ___ that everyone in the room laughed.

def: keeping careful watch for possible danger or trouble; alert
ex: Lifeguards must stay vigilant, scanning the water even when the beach is quiet.
Banks urge customers to be vigilant about suspicious emails asking for passwords.

cloze.s: Parents at the busy playground stayed ___, never taking their eyes off their toddlers.

def: strange or mysterious in a way that is hard to explain, often unsettlingly so
ex: Maria bears an uncanny resemblance to her grandmother at the same age.
Hannah has an uncanny ability to guess which song the radio will play next.

cloze.s: The robot's face looked so lifelike that many visitors found it ___ and a little creepy.

def: causing or likely to cause heated argument; strongly disputed
ex: The budget meeting was contentious, with members shouting over one another.
Ownership of the land remains a contentious question in the courts.

cloze.s: After a long and ___ divorce, the couple communicated only through their lawyers.

also: Of a person: inclined to start arguments.

def: not aware of or not noticing what is happening around you
ex: Absorbed in his phone, Liam was oblivious to the bus pulling away.
The tourists seemed oblivious to the rising tide creeping up behind them.

cloze.s: Wearing noise-canceling headphones, Priya was completely ___ to the fire alarm ringing down the hall.

def: too pleased with yourself and your achievements, in a way that irritates others
ex: After winning the bet, Diego wore a smug grin for the rest of the evening.

cloze.s: He gave a ___ little smirk when the boss praised his report in front of the coworkers he'd beaten.

def: refusing to be persuaded or to change your mind; completely firm
ex: Kwame was adamant that he had locked the door before leaving.
The organizers remained adamant that the festival would go ahead despite the rain.

cloze.s: Despite her friends' pleas, Hannah was ___ that she would not attend the reunion.

def: causing a strong feeling of sadness or tender emotion that touches the heart
ex: The letter from her late father was a poignant reminder of his love.
The documentary ends with a poignant scene of refugees returning to their ruined village.

cloze.s: Seeing the empty chair at the holiday table was a ___ moment for the grieving family.

def: not secure or stable, and therefore likely to fall, fail, or become dangerous
ex: The vase sat in a precarious position at the very edge of the shelf.

cloze.s: The hikers inched along a ___ ledge with a sheer drop on one side.

def: showing extreme care about every small detail; very precise and thorough
ex: Wei kept meticulous records of every expense for her tax return.
Restoring the damaged painting required meticulous work over many months.

cloze.s: The surgeon was known for her ___ attention to detail, checking every stitch twice.

def: harmful in a way that develops slowly and quietly, so it is hard to notice
ex: High blood pressure is insidious because it often causes no symptoms for years.

cloze.s: The damage from the slow leak was ___, rotting the floor beams long before anyone saw a stain.

def: silly or not serious; lacking real purpose or value
ex: Aisha cut back on frivolous purchases like designer phone cases.
The judge dismissed the lawsuit as frivolous and ordered the plaintiff to pay costs.

cloze.s: With rent due tomorrow, buying a third pair of sunglasses seemed ___.

def: able to express ideas clearly, skillfully, and persuasively, especially when speaking
ex: Fatima gave an eloquent speech that moved many of the wedding guests to tears.
The novelist wrote an eloquent essay about growing up between two languages.

cloze.s: The student's ___ speech persuaded the entire school board to change the rule.

def: too satisfied with your situation to notice dangers or to try to improve
ex: After three easy wins, the team grew complacent and lost to the last-place club.

cloze.s: Years without a break-in made the store owner ___, and he stopped locking the back door.

note: Not the same as *complaisant*, which means eager to please.

def: so intense or obvious that it can almost be felt or touched
ex: The tension in the courtroom was palpable as the jury returned.

cloze.s: When the layoffs were announced, the fear in the office was ___; no one spoke above a whisper.

also: In medicine, able to be felt by touch, as in 'a palpable lump.'

def: requiring great effort, energy, and endurance; very difficult and tiring
ex: The arduous climb to the summit took the group nine hours.

cloze.s: Getting the visa meant months of ___ paperwork, interviews, and waiting in long lines.

def: large, heavy, or complicated, and therefore difficult to carry, use, or manage
ex: The old printer was too cumbersome to carry up the stairs alone.

cloze.s: The bulky, ___ winter coat made it hard for Yuki to squeeze into her airplane seat.

def: involving only the most basic or simple elements; not developed or advanced
ex: Olga has a rudimentary knowledge of Korean, enough to order food and say thank you.

cloze.s: With only ___ tools, the stranded sailors built a shelter from driftwood and rope.

def: quick to understand situations accurately and use them to your advantage; shrewd
ex: An astute investor, Jamal sold his shares just before the market dropped.
The detective made an astute observation about the muddy boots by the door.

cloze.s: The ___ shopper noticed that the 'sale' price was actually higher than last week's regular price.

def: careful to spend little money and avoid waste
ex: Being frugal, Tomas packs his lunch instead of eating out every day.
Their frugal habits allowed the couple to pay off their mortgage early.

cloze.s: My ___ grandmother saved every rubber band and reused aluminum foil until it tore.

note: Usually positive; *stingy* or *cheap* is the negative way to describe the same habit.

def: firmly determined to do something and not willing to give up or waver
ex: Despite her sore knee, Priya was resolute about finishing the marathon.
The firefighters showed resolute courage throughout the long night.

cloze.s: Facing loud protests from parents, the principal remained ___ in her decision to ban phones in class.

def: with great energy, force, and enthusiasm
ex: Hannah scrubbed the burned pan vigorously until it shone.
The company vigorously denied the reports of unsafe working conditions.

cloze.s: Shake the bottle ___ for thirty seconds so the oil and vinegar mix completely.

def: in a clear, simple, and direct way that is easy to see or understand
ex: The doctor explained the diagnosis plainly, without any confusing jargon.
The exit sign was plainly visible from every seat in the theater.

cloze.s: Please speak ___ and skip the technical terms; I just want to know if the roof needs replacing.

def: definitely and noticeably; to a degree that is clear to everyone
ex: The weather was decidedly cooler after the storm passed.
Kwame was decidedly unimpressed by the twenty-dollar sandwich.

cloze.s: The second half of the season went ___ worse for the team, with eight losses in a row.

note: Not the same as *decisively*, which means in a firm way that settles something.

def: in a way that is widely known for something bad or unfavorable
ex: The mountain road is notoriously dangerous in winter.

cloze.s: That airline is ___ unreliable; its flights are delayed more often than not.

note: Unlike *famously*, it implies a bad reputation.

def: as it appears or is claimed on the surface, though possibly not truly
ex: He visited ostensibly to return a book, but he really wanted to borrow money.
The meeting was ostensibly about budgets, yet it focused entirely on layoffs.

cloze.s: The trip was ___ for business, but Malik spent most of it at the beach.

def: barely; almost not at all, or only just
ex: Sofia could scarcely believe she had won the scholarship.
There was scarcely enough food left for the last guests to arrive.

cloze.s: The fog was so thick that we could ___ see the car in front of us.

note: Like *hardly*, it already has a negative sense, so avoid 'couldn't scarcely.'

def: in a very obvious and shameless way, usually about something wrong
ex: The player blatantly tripped his opponent right in front of the referee.
The new ad blatantly copied a rival company's slogan.

cloze.s: The student ___ copied his neighbor's answers while the teacher stood right beside him.

def: without stopping, slowing down, or becoming less intense
ex: Rain fell relentlessly for three days, flooding the basement.
Aisha practiced relentlessly until she could play the whole sonata from memory.

cloze.s: The reporters pursued the story ___, calling sources every single day for months.

def: in a way that cannot be doubted or disputed; certainly
ex: It was unquestionably the best meal Liam had eaten all year.
The new bridge is unquestionably safer than the crumbling one it replaced.

cloze.s: With twelve gold medals, she is ___ the greatest swimmer in the country's history.

def: in a forceful, passionate, and intense way, especially when disagreeing
ex: Olga vehemently opposed the plan to cut the library's hours.
The singer vehemently denied the rumors about her retirement.

cloze.s: Residents protested ___ against the new highway, shouting and waving signs at the council meeting.

def: in a way that is suitable or fitting for the situation
ex: The black cat, aptly named Shadow, followed Wei everywhere she went.
Tomas aptly described the chaotic week as 'controlled panic.'

cloze.s: The dog, which never stops eating, is ___ named Muncher.

def: in a hesitant or uncertain way, or as a plan that is not yet final
ex: The meeting is tentatively scheduled for Thursday at noon.
Yuki tentatively dipped a toe into the icy lake.

cloze.s: The shy new student raised her hand ___, unsure whether her answer was right.

def: to make it harder for someone or something to make progress or happen
ex: Heavy snow hindered rescue efforts in the mountains.
Lack of sleep can hinder your ability to concentrate at work.

cloze.s: Constant interruptions from his phone ___ Jamal's progress on the report all afternoon.

def: to escape from or avoid something or someone, often by cleverness or trickery
ex: The suspect evaded police for three weeks before being caught.

cloze.s: The company tried to ___ taxes by hiding its profits in overseas accounts.

def: to feel bitter or angry about something you think is unfair
ex: Maria resented being blamed for a mistake she didn't make.

cloze.s: He ___ his brother for getting the bigger bedroom and complained about it for years.

def: to be better, greater, or more than someone or something; exceed
ex: Ticket sales surpassed all expectations on opening weekend.
Hannah hopes to surpass her personal best in next month's race.

cloze.s: By noon, the temperature had ___ 100 degrees for the first time this year.

def: to say the opposite of what someone has said, or to be inconsistent with something
ex: The witness's story contradicted the security camera footage.
Kwame never contradicts his boss in front of clients, even when she is wrong.

cloze.s: The new study ___ earlier findings, showing that the drug had no effect at all.

def: to become, or make something become, greater, more serious, or more intense
ex: A minor argument over parking escalated into a shouting match.
When the refund didn't arrive, Priya escalated her complaint to a senior manager.

cloze.s: Officials feared the border dispute would ___ into a full-scale war.

def: to think about something carefully and for a long time
ex: Diego pondered the job offer for a week before accepting.
Philosophers have pondered the meaning of life for thousands of years.

cloze.s: She sat by the window, quietly ___ whether to move across the country.

def: to consider or judge something to be a certain way, often officially
ex: The building was deemed unsafe after the earthquake.

cloze.s: The referee ___ the goal invalid because of an earlier foul.

note: Formal; often passive, as in 'was deemed necessary.'

def: to cause something unpleasant or painful, such as harm or damage, to someone or something
ex: The storm inflicted serious damage on the coastal towns.

cloze.s: The hailstorm ___ thousands of dollars of damage on the cars in the lot.

note: Not the same as *afflict*: you inflict pain on someone, but a disease afflicts a person.
